title: Verify air-gapped upgrade bundles via SHA256 manifest + signature; improve missing/incorrect artifact errors
author: Fatima Noor
description: Context: Design partners and Support have hit confusing failures in the offline/air-gapped upgrade flow when bundles are incomplete, corrupted, or built against the wrong target version (see SUP-18510). Today the installer will often fail late (during image/chart pull) and the error doesn’t clearly tell the operator what’s missing or mismatched. This PR adds deterministic bundle verification up front: (1) a required SHA256 checksum manifest for all bundle artifacts, (2) optional signature verification for the manifest, and (3) clearer, actionable error messages that enumerate missing/incorrect artifacts before any cluster mutations. Behavior: - New required file inside bundle: bundle.manifest.json (list of artifacts + expected sha256 + size + logical type). - New required file inside bundle: bundle.manifest.sha256 (sha256sum of bundle.manifest.json) OR embedded sha256 in the manifest (we accept either; prefer sha256 file). - Optional files: bundle.manifest.sig + bundle.manifest.pub (ed25519). If present, installer verifies signature and prints signer fingerprint. (Signature is optional for this release to avoid breaking existing customers; we will gate to required in a future major). - Installer runs verification during upgrade plan generation and again immediately before apply (defense-in-depth if bundle is swapped between plan/apply). - Error messaging: missing artifact(s) are printed as a numbered list with expected paths; checksum mismatch prints expected vs actual sha256 and suggests re-download/re-mirror; version mismatch prints bundle target version vs requested version and points to the compatibility policy doc. - Adds break-glass flag: --skip-bundle-verification (hidden behind --i-understand-the-risks) for Support-only workflows. Security notes: No secrets are stored in the bundle verification metadata. Public key is optional and can be provided via file path or embedded in the bundle. Logging: verification results are included in the installer run summary and emitted as a structured event (bundle_verify_started / bundle_verify_failed / bundle_verify_succeeded). Testing: unit tests cover manifest parsing, sha validation, signature verification, and error formatting; integration test adds a corrupted bundle fixture and asserts failure before any k8s writes. Rollout: This is backward compatible for existing bundles (signature optional; checksum manifest required only when --airgapped-bundle is used). For online installs nothing changes. Checklist: - [x] Verify missing chart/image entries are surfaced preflight - [x] Verify corrupted tarball errors are actionable - [x] Add docs snippet to installer help output - [x] Add integration fixture + CI lane
commits: installer/airgap: introduce BundleVerifier and manifest types
airgap: sha256 verification + better error reporting for missing/mismatched artifacts
airgap: optional ed25519 signature verification for manifest (bundle.manifest.sig)
tests: add corrupted bundle fixture + unit tests for signature/sha parsing
logging: emit structured bundle verification events in run summary
changed_areas: docs/cli-help.md (update installer help text for new files/flags)
conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we fail before we even start k8s interactions? We had a case where the bundle was missing the chart tgz and it only showed up during Helm. Also please ensure the error includes the expected relative path so Support can tell customers exactly what to mirror.

Fatima Noor (author): Yes — verification now runs as part of plan generation (no k8s writes) and again right before apply. Error output enumerates expected paths from the manifest. Added a dedicated error formatter so it’s consistent with other preflight output.

Marcus Lin: Signature verification: what’s the trust model here? If signature is optional, we should at least strongly warn when a signature is present but invalid. Also, don’t allow arbitrary key fetch from network in airgapped mode.

Fatima Noor (author): Agreed. If .sig exists and verification fails, we hard-fail (no fallback). If no signature files, we proceed with sha validation only and print a warning that integrity is checked but provenance is not. Public key is only loaded from a local path or from bundle.manifest.pub if provided; no network access.

Irene Choi: For on-prem, operators will ask how to generate the sha/manifest. Are we providing a generator script or just validating? Also what about large bundles—streaming verification vs reading into memory?

Fatima Noor (author): This PR validates only; bundle creation is handled by the release pipeline (separate PR). Verification streams file hashing from disk (io.Copy to sha256) and does not load artifacts into memory. Added notes in help text describing required files and that they are produced by Redwood’s release tooling.
Victor Alvarez: Minor: the error for ‘missing registry mirror endpoint’ should not show up for offline bundles; it confused one of our staging tests.
Fatima Noor (author): Good catch. I scoped mirror endpoint checks to online mode only; airgapped verification now focuses strictly on bundle presence/integrity.
Connor O'Brien: Approved once the break-glass flag is behind a scary prompt / explicit acknowledgment.
Fatima Noor (author): Implemented --skip-bundle-verification only with --i-understand-the-risks, plus it prints a big warning and is excluded from normal help output.
Connor O'Brien: Approved. Please add a note in release notes for Support.
release_notes: Private/on-prem: Air-gapped upgrade bundles are now verified pre-upgrade via SHA256 manifest; optional manifest signature verification is supported.
Installer errors for missing/incorrect offline artifacts are now actionable and list the exact missing paths and checksum mismatches.
Support-only: Added break-glass flags to bypass verification with explicit risk acknowledgment.
